subject: Oct payout hold — AWS hourly overlap causing duplicate metering + EU VAT passback
messages:
From: Tia Summers <tia.summers@cloudlayer-retail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@cloudlayer-retail.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Oct payout hold — suspected duplicate metering impacting EU VAT passback

Hi Karthik / Laura,

We just received the October payout statement and noticed a ~€82k withholding flagged as "duplicate metering" for services delivered in the EU. Our finance team traced it to a set of AWS Marketplace SKUs that show overlapping hourly usage windows between 22:00-23:00 UTC on 2027-10-31 — effectively double-counted across two entity IDs. We've attached a CSV export of our internal usage and a screenshot from our GCP mirror showing the window alignment.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether you see the same duplicate hourly stamps on your marketplace ingest?
- Can you provide the marketplace usage export(s) that were used to calculate the payout adjustment?
- We also need confirmation on how VAT was applied to the withheld amount (CloudLayer is EU-registered and expects VAT passback treatment).

This withholding is blocking our month-end close; can we expedite? If useful we can hop on a short call today.

Thanks,
Tia Summers
Head of Billing, CloudLayer Retail
T: +44 20 5555 0101
Files: cloudlayer_oct_usage_202710.csv (CSV), gcp-mirror-window-snapshot-20271031.png (PNG)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tia Summers <tia.summers@cloudlayer-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Oct payout hold — suspected duplicate metering impacting EU VAT passback

Hi Tia — thanks for the note and the artifacts. Sorry to hear this is causing a close delay. Looping in Marissa (finance ops) and Laura (billing) so we can assemble the marketplace evidence and the VAT treatment detail.

Initial plan:
- Laura will pull the AWS/GCP marketplace usage exports and the ledger lines that fed into the Oct settlement.
- Marissa will review payout logic and confirm whether a manual credit was issued or if this was an automatic withholding by marketplace escrow.
- I will coordinate with our tax team and with AWS contacts to confirm VAT passback eligibility for the withheld amount.

Can you confirm the buyer entity IDs you believe were double-counted and whether the usage in question is limited to that single SKU family? Also: is CloudLayer registered for EU VAT in both DE and NL? That will change routing.

I'll aim to share the first set of marketplace exports by EOD tomorrow (Wed 2027-11-03). If you'd like a 30-min troubleshooting call, propose 2027-11-03 08:00-08:30 UTC.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: urgent — CloudLayer duplicate-hour hold (EU VAT impact)

Marissa / Laura — short summary and request: CloudLayer reports a €82k withholding on Oct settlement flagged as duplicate metering across AWS SKUs with overlapping hourly stamps 22:00-23:00 UTC 2027-10-31. They provided the attached CSV and a GCP snapshot (they mirror some workloads to GCP).

What I need:
1) Laura — pull the marketplace usage exports (AWS Marketplace usage report and GCP marketplace if applicable) and the settlement invoice that produced the withheld line. Include raw event timestamps (UTC), SKU ids, and buyer entity IDs.
2) Marissa — check whether this was:
   - an automated withholding originated by AWS Marketplace (i.e., marketplace escrow) OR
   - a Redwood-initiated credit hold due to ledger mismatch.
If it's marketplace escrow, we need marketplace contact and the exact escrow reference so CloudLayer can claim via AWS — and a proposal for interim credit if Redwood can front it.
3) Both — coordinate with tax (cc: tax@redwood.ai) on EU VAT passback: is the withheld amount treated as a taxable supply subject to passback, or withheld as a settlement correction where VAT was already remitted upstream?

Deadlines: please have the raw exports + short summary in my inbox by Wed 2027-11-03 17:00 UTC. If you run into red flags, escalate to me immediately. I'll schedule a call with CloudLayer once we have the exports.

Karthik

From: Tia Summers <tia.summers@cloudlayer-retail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 07:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Oct payout hold — suspected duplicate metering impacting EU VAT passback

Thanks Karthik — confirming the buyer entity IDs we flagged in the CSV: CL-EU-DE-01 and CL-EU-NL-02. The spike is limited to SKU family cl-vm-highmem-ssd. We are EU VAT-registered in DE only (CL-EU-DE-01); NL entity is a passthrough.

I've attached the CSV again and included a short slice showing the overlapping hourly stamps. We can do the 2027-11-03 08:00-08:30 UTC slot — I booked it on your calendar (invite should show up).

Attachments: cloudlayer_oct_usage_202710.csv, gcp-mirror-window-snapshot-20271031.png

Tia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tia Summers <tia.summers@cloudlayer-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Oct payout hold — suspected duplicate metering impacting EU VAT passback

Tia — quick update and mutual action plan following today's call (notes below). Thanks for the materials and patience.

Summary of findings (high level):
- Marketplace exports show two ingest events for the cl-vm-highmem-ssd SKU with identical timestamps at hour boundary 22:00 UTC that were attributed to two separate buyer entity IDs in AWS's ledger. This aligns with your CSV.
- AWS has confirmed the ledger entries are denormalized at settlement and flagged the line as a duplicate adjustment. The withholding was applied by AWS marketplace escrow, not a Redwood-initiated hold.
- Tax team: the withheld amount was classified as a settlement correction; AWS has indicated VAT was not re-allocated to the buyer at time of adjustment. CloudLayer provided VAT registration for DE (CL-EU-DE-01) which should qualify for passback.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) AWS action (we opened ticket AWS-87291): AWS to correct ledger attribution or provide formal adjustment confirmation to release escrow. Target: AWS commit by 2027-11-12.
2) Redwood deliverables:
   - Laura to send the raw marketplace export and the settlement ledger lines we pulled (attached: aws-invoice-987654.pdf, raw-usage-export-aws-20271031.csv). Due: 2027-11-10 16:00 UTC.
   - Marissa to prepare an interim credit proposal for CloudLayer to bridge cashflow if AWS timing slips >7 days. Proposal expected by 2027-11-11.
3) CloudLayer action: provide signed VAT registration excerpt for CL-EU-DE-01 to support VAT passback claim (they provided already; submit official certificate via AWS portal).
4) Tax: confirm final VAT routing once AWS issues formal adjustment.

If AWS fails to provide formal adjustment by 2027-11-12, Marissa's interim credit will be triggered per the agreed proposal. We'll keep you updated in this thread and via the Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-4821.

Attachments included: aws-invoice-987654.pdf, cloudlayer_oct_usage_202710.csv, gcp-mirror-window-snapshot-20271031.png

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
